text:
Maria D.: Hey team — hitting this from a customer using our Python SDK behind a corp proxy doing TLS inspection. SDK calls fail with: 
```
requests.exceptions.SSLError: [SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED] certificate verify failed: unable to get local issuer certificate (_ssl.c:1007)
```
Anyone seen this pattern and best fix? They're not willing to disable proxy inspection.

Ajay P.: Which SDK version + Python? also, are they using REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE or certifi?

Maria D.: python3.10, redwood-python v0.9.2. They say not setting anything special — default install. Error happens when hitting streaming endpoints and normal generate endpoints.

Sophie L.: Classic corporate MITM. Two routes: (1) give the app the corporate CA chain (set REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE or SSL_CERT_FILE env var) or (2) point the SDK client config verify param at a vendor-provided CA file. Example env: `export REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE=/etc/corp/ca-bundle.pem`

Sophie L.: Quick debug trick: `openssl s_client -showcerts -connect api.redwood.example.com:443 -servername api.redwood.example.com` — run that from inside the customer's environment to see the presented chain. If the proxy inserts its cert, you'll see it in the output.

Maria D.: tried instructing them to set REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE but they say streaming still drops intermittently (handshake ok but then short read / unexpected EOF during stream). Stack shows `SSLError: [SSL: WRONG_VERSION_NUMBER] wrong version number` in some cases.

Kevin H.: If proxy is terminating TLS and re-encrypting, it can break HTTP/2 or connection reuse semantics. Do you know if they're using HTTP/2 / SSE / gRPC? Our Python SDK uses SSE for streaming by default right now. Some corporate proxies don't like long-lived HTTP/1.1 chunked or HTTP/2 streams.

Ajay P.: For Python requests + SSE the combo is: requests -> urllib3 -> raw socket. If the proxy mangles ALPN or downgrades, you'll see odd errors. Try forcing HTTP/1.1 or disabling HTTP/2 where applicable. Also check NODE/Java equivalents: Node uses `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` for custom CA.

Sophie L.: Also confirm they have the full CA chain in their bundle. Missing intermediate CA can cause intermittent verification failures depending on which proxy/cache node they're hitting. `curl -v https://api.redwood.example.com --cacert /etc/corp/ca-bundle.pem` should return 200 and show cert chain.

Maria D.: here's the minimal repro they ran in their environment (they gave this to me):
```
import requests
resp = requests.get('https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/stream', stream=True)
for line in resp.iter_lines():
    print(line)
```
They say adding `verify='/etc/corp/ca-bundle.pem'` fixes the immediate SSLError but streaming still sometimes fails after a few seconds.

Kevin H.: Two things to try: (1) disable connection pooling/reuse for streams (requests' session mounting) so each stream uses a fresh TCP/TLS handshake. Some proxies mishandle reuse. (2) Force `Connection: close` for stream requests as a workaround.

Ajay P.: Another angle: mTLS? Are they doing any client cert injection at the proxy? If the proxy tries to present client certs it can confuse the server. But if they only do inspection it's usually server cert replacement.

Sophie L.: If they can run `openssl s_client -connect api.redwood.example.com:443 -tls1_2 -servername api.redwood.example.com -showcerts` from inside their network and paste output that will tell us if the proxy is fiddling with ALPN/h2. If ALPN isn't showing h2 then HTTP/2 won't work.

Maria D.: asked them to run openssl and curl. They pasted curl verbose, shows `ALPN, server accepted to use http/1.1` — so it seems proxy strips h2. Stacktrace shows chunked body truncated sometimes.

Kevin H.: In that case, try forcing HTTP/1.1 in the SDK so client and proxy agree. For requests you can set header `Connection: keep-alive` and `Accept: text/event-stream` but if proxy kills long connections you'd still see truncation. The short-term pragmatic fix is to increase reconnect logic in the SDK stream client: resume on disconnect with idempotent tokens.

Ajay P.: SDK-side config example (python):
```
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=..., tls_verify='/etc/corp/ca-bundle.pem', stream_reconnect=True, stream_retries=5)
```
We don't actually have `tls_verify` in v0.9.2 — can we add a `verify` passthrough? @Maria D. can you file a tiny PR to let the client accept a `verify` path/env?

Maria D.: I can. I want to add docs too: a short troubleshooting note for corp proxies (REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE, NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS, force http1, reconnect). I'll make a branch and ping for review.

Sophie L.: Also add a snippet showing how to inspect the chain with `openssl` and `curl -v`. Helpful to include example error strings so customers can search.

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: devex/docs-tls-fixes -> staging at 2024-11-14T16:30:00Z :rocket: (automated note)

Maria D.: Thanks — I'll push a small PR in ~30m and ping @Ajay P. for review. If anyone has a copy/paste of a `requests` adapter workaround to force fresh connections for streams, drop it here.

Kevin H.: Quick adapter snippet:
```
from requests.adapters import HTTPAdapter
from urllib3.util import Retry
s = requests.Session()
s.mount('https://', HTTPAdapter(pool_connections=1, pool_maxsize=1, max_retries=Retry(total=3)))
# and set Connection: close on stream requests
```
That helps if pooling is the culprit.

Ajay P.: Good. Also note in docs that corporate TLS interception can break HTTP/2 and long-lived SSE/gRPC. Recommend customers either install the corp CA into the runtime trust store or use our Dedicated/private option for network isolation.

Maria D.: Perfect — creating PR now. Will include troubleshooting checklist and the adapter snippet. Thanks all :heart:
